High-level proposal (summary):

- Data plane: Runs in customer VPC (Acme), hosts model-serving nodes and holds KV caches. Communicates with control plane over an authenticated gRPC bridge; all egress restricted to specific Redwood IP ranges.

2) Confirm how mutual auth and key rotation will be handled in customer's KMS.

Ravi — good questions. Short answers and notes (high level):

HA / failover behavior:
- In-flight requests: model-serving in the data plane continues to serve from local KV/cache while control plane is unreachable. Any calls that require control-plane-only actions (e.g., model rollout triggers, billing events) will queue locally and replay when the bridge is back up. We implement idempotent replay.
- KV consistency: we do not assume synchronous writes to central control plane. The data plane maintains local state and periodic reconciliation is performed via the bridge. For critical metadata, we use a write-ahead log replicated to Redwood's ingestion endpoint when connectivity resumes.

Connectivity options:
- Preferred: Private VPC peering or AWS Transit Gateway attachment to Redwood's dedicated peering fabric (recommended for strict egress controls).
- Alternative: NAT'ed egress to a small set of static IP ranges (we publish a /28 block per region) over TLS with mTLS for auth.

Auth & key rotation:
- We support mTLS with client certs + a KMS-backed signing key for rotation. Customer can hold the KMS key and rotate certs on a monthly cadence; Redwood supports cert pinning via thumbprint.

Ops/runbook (short checklist appended):
- Pre-deploy: network ACLs, route table entries, KMS access policy, security group openings (TCP 443 for control gRPC, ICMP for health probes if requested).
- Deploy: bootstrap data-plane nodes with our agent, establish bridge, run smoke requests, verify KV reconciliation.
- Post-deploy: enable tracing, validate cost telemetry, set capacity alerts.

I've added an ops-runbook.md to the internal draft (attachment). Monica/Vivek — can you confirm the APM/alert thresholds?

Quick security notes after scanning the draft diagram and checklist:

1) KMS & key material: we prefer customer-managed KMS for the cert private keys. We'll need a policy template for least-privilege access and an agreed rotation window. Add this to the runbook.

2) Audit logs: for compliance (SOX/ISO) Acme requested 90-day immutable logs for control-plane auth events. Redwood can stream auth audit events into the customer's S3/GCS bucket; we'll add an ACL/landing prefix pattern to the checklist.

3) Network hardening: require that the customer implement strict security group rules (source: Redwood IP CIDRs only) and enable VPC Flow Logs + GuardDuty for suspicious egress. We'll include a firewall template — Elena, if EdgeCloud has a curated template for Transit Gateway + peering, can you drop it here?

4) Minimal exposure: do not open SSH from the internet to data-plane nodes; if remote support is needed we'll use a short-lived access token and ephemeral bastion via the control plane.

I updated the Confluence page: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Private+VPC+ControlPlane+Runbook (see the KMS and audit sections).
